# Lowest-supported direct dependency profile for CPython 3.9 on Linux.
#
# This file is what makes setup.py's lower bounds real. A floor nothing
# installs is a promise nothing keeps, so the "Minimum dependencies" job in
# .github/workflows/tests.yml installs exactly this profile and runs the same
# suite the newest-resolution job runs. setup.py's dependency-policy block
# states the rule; this file is the half that executes it.
#
# EVERY PIN HERE EQUALS THE FLOOR setup.py DECLARES, and the exceptions are
# listed below by name. That is not tidiness: a pin sitting quietly above its
# floor means the floor is the one bound in setup.py that nothing tests, and
# the version a pinned user's resolver lands on is the version CI skipped.
# tests/test_optimal_dependency_versions.py rejects an unexplained gap.
#
# Most exceptions are packages whose floors cannot be installed together, so
# the profile takes the first mutually installable set instead:
#   torch 2.1.0 + torchvision 0.16.0 require sympy 1.12;
#   umap-learn 0.5.11 requires scikit-learn 1.6 or newer;
#   tensorboard 2.21.0 requires protobuf 6.31.1 or newer.
#
# nvidia-ml-py IS NOT AN EXCEPTION, and the pin is not a typo. It numbers
# each release after the NVIDIA driver it binds -- 10.418.84, 11.450.51,
# 11.460.79, ..., 13.610.43 -- so the middle field is a driver branch and
# 11.450.51 sorts ABOVE a plausible-looking 11.5. A round lower bound such as
# `>=11.5` therefore names no release this distribution will ever publish,
# and a floor that cannot be equalled is a floor this profile cannot pin.
# setup.py declares `>=11.450.51` for that reason and this pin equals it; the
# two spellings admit the same published releases, so the choice is about
# whether the bound names a version, not about which versions resolve.
#
# cellpose is pinned at setup.py's floor, 4.0.7, NOT at the first published
# 4.x. This file used to pin 4.0.1 on the reasoning that it was the first 4.x
# release, which stopped being the point when the floor was raised:
# CellposeModel's signature differs between them (use_bfloat16 absent in
# 4.0.1, resample defaulting True rather than None), so the job was
# installing a version the package declares it does not support and failing
# ~23 tests that pass on every other job.
#
# statsmodels and shap were once the same failure in the other direction: the
# pin matched setup.py exactly and SETUP.PY was the file that was wrong.
# 0.13.5 and 0.45.0 were floors nobody had run, and this job is what ran them
# -- 16 failures no other job had, all of them an API spaCR uses that the
# pinned release does not have. setup.py now declares statsmodels>=0.14.0 and
# shap>=0.47.0 with the reason written next to each, and
# tests/test_dependency_floors_have_the_api.py keeps the two facts joined.
# Both versions publish cp39 wheels.
#
# Dependencies with no declared lower bound (czifile and readlif) are left to
# pip. This file constrains direct dependencies only; transitive packages are
# resolved normally so their own compatibility metadata remains
# authoritative.

# purpose is that nothing floats.
